output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise is not a handling problem. Bags that fail automatic tag reading go to the manual encode desk and arrive at the make-up lateral after it closes. Corvane's no-read rate jumped from 1.5% to 11.8% for tags printed on the new Fennick stock from 1 Sep. Corvane transfer tags and Pelion tags, read by the same equipment, stayed at about 1.3–1.4%. Pelion is also handled by Tessaly's single crew pool, and its mishandling rate did not change. Corvane bags that were read automatically still mishandle at the old rate. All the extra misses are on the encode path, and 91% of those arrived after lateral closing. On 14–16 Oct, counters using Brackwater stock from stores failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock failed at 12.1% on the same days. The stock change is therefore the cause. I can't yet say whether the stock is defective or whether printer heat settings need adjusting. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now, since it is in stores and valid to 31 Dec. Test Fennick separately, including printer settings, before any claim against Fennick. Hold the Tessaly notice and fee withholding. Optionally ask HBAA for a temporary extra encode workstation in the evening bank.
